גדלתי באותו מסגרת כנסייתית שבה נולדו וגדלו הוריי. אולם עד שהגעתי לגיל 10, הוריי החלו לדאוג לכיוון שאליו נוטים הצעירים ורצו משהו שונה לילדיהם. לכן, הוריי יצרו קשר עם כנסייה ממדינה אחרת, שעזרה להם ליצור קשרים עם כנסייה קטנה שהייתה קרובה למקום שבו גרנו.

הייתי ילד שקט ובעקשן במהותו והפכתי במהרה לנער מרדני. הוריי עשו כל מה שהם ידעו לעשות איתי באותה תקופה. אחד הדברים היה המעבר לכנסייה החדשה הזאת, מאחר שהייתה בה סביבה נעורים אדוקה יותר. לי היה קשה עם השינוי הזה. בכנסייה הישנה היו לי חברים שחשבו כמוני ותמכו בדרכי המרדנית, אך בכנסייה החדשה הייתי יותר ה"בן הרע" ולא התאימותי עם שאר הצעירים.

במהלך הזמן אותה כנסייה התפוררה, והורי החליטו לעבור למדינה אחרת, קרוב יותר לכנסייה יציבה יותר. כך היה, שכשהגעתי לגיל 14, בילינו את הלילה הראשון שלנו במדינה אחרת, בבית שונה, ברחוב שונה, ועם שכנים שונים. קנינו בעיר אחרת והלכנו לכנסייה אחרת, עם אנשים שהכרתי בקושי. לא אהבתי שינוי. מצאתי שאתגר לי לפגוש אנשים חדשים וליצור חברויות חדשות. נאבקתי קשות עם כל השינויים האלה, אז לא טרחתי לנסות להשתלב ולהיות חלק פעיל בחיי החדשים. במקום זאת, בניתי לאט קירות סביב חיי ולבי, תוך שאני הופך קר יותר ומרדני יותר.

ככל שהתקדמתי בגיל והתקשחתי, הוריי ניסו להתמודד איתי, אך לא רציתי שום דבר מזה. לבסוף קיבלתי עבודה והוכחתי למוזיקת קאנטרי ולדברים אחרים מהעולם. מאחר שנהניתי לעבוד, הטמעתי את עצמי בזה ועבדתי שעות רבות. כך לא הייתי צריך להיות בקרבת המשפחה או אנשי הכנסייה, ולא הייתי צריך ללכת לפעילויות כנסייתיות. לכן התרחקתי ובודדתי את עצמי מאחרים סביבי.

אנשי הכנסייה לא ידעו כיצד להתחבר אלי; רובם פשוט השאירו אותי לעצמי. עמוק בפנים נרקדתי רצון עז לאהבה ולקבלה מהמשפחה ומהכנסייה. זה גרם לי להידרדר. המשכתי לדחוס את רגשותיי ולבנות קיר סביבי, בזמן שלבי התקשה עוד יותר. עם הזמן, התרחקתי יותר ויותר מהמשפחה ומהכנסייה. הרגשתי יותר ויותר כמי שאינו משתלב חברתית ושאף אחד לא יודע מה לעשות עמו. החלטתי שאני הולך לברוח ולחיות את חיי בעצמי.

באופן כלשהו הוריי קלטו את הרעיון הזה וניסו לעשות כל מה שהם ידעו לעשות כדי לעזור לי, אך שמרתי טינה על כך. כשאני מסתכל אחורה, אני יודע ללא ספק שהם עשו זאת מתוך אהבה ודאגה, אך היה חוסר גדול בקשר בינינו. לכן המשכתי להתקשות ולהתקפא.

בקיץ שבו הייתי בן 17, נזיר מבקר ("מייק") ומשפחתו באו לכנסייתנו לפגישות. הכרתי אותם משנים קודם לכן ובאופן כלשהו דרך אינטראקציה שלנו במהלך הפגישות לבי החל להתרכך ולהיפתח. אינני לגמרי בטוח מדוע, אך מסיבה כלשהי החלטתי שאני רוצה ללכת ולבלות את החורף אצלם. אז, הוריי יצרו קשר איתם, והוחלט שאוכל להישאר אצלם כמה חודשים.

התוכנית שלי הייתה להעביר כמה חודשים הרחק מהכל ואז לשוב הביתה כשתהיה לי כמעט 18. ברגע שאהיה בן 18 הייתה כוונתי לעזוב את הבית ולעשות את דרכי. הייתי בטוח שאף אחד לא יכול לעצור אותי כי אהיה בגיל החוקי. אולם,显然 לאלה היו תוכניות שונות...

באופן כלשהו "מייק" שכנע אותי להצטרף לשבוע פגישות במדינה אחרת. בזמן שהיינו שם, אינני זוכר שהשכנוע (החטיפה המוסרית) היה חזק יותר מאשר בכל פעם אחרת. אולם, בערב אחד אחרי השירות הוא שאל אותי אם רציתי להיות נוצרי ולקבל מחילה על חטאי. אינני זוכר מה עניתי לו, אך שוחחנו זמן מה. הוא הוביל אותי דרך הברית החדשה, עוזר לי לראות מה אלוהים אומר על כל זה; ואז התפללנו. כשקמנו מהתפילה, אינני יכול לומר שמשהו גדול קרה, אבל זו בוודאות הייתה הלילה שבו מצאתי את הישועה! באותו לילה משהו השתנה בלבי. ידעתי שמעכשיו אני רוצה לעשות את רצון ה'. ידעתי שמטרת הסיום בחיי היא לרוץ את המרוץ היטב ולסיים בניצחון. זה מה שעזר לי לאורך השנים.

ב-31 ביולי 2011 נטבלתי על סמך הודאת אמונתי. השנים שאחר כך בהחלט לא היו קלות. אפילו אומר שלפעמים זה נראה שקשה יותר מאשר בשנים לפני התשובה שלי. מתוך כבוד לאחרים, אינני מרגיש שיכול לשתף הכל שאירע במהלך השנים, אך אשתדל לשתף כמה נקודות עיקריות. אפשר לדמיין שבעזרת הקירות שבניתי סביבי והנוחות שמצאתי בזה, השנים שאחרי תשובתי היו מלאות עליות ומורדות כשניסיתי ללמוד מחדש כיצד לקשר עם מאמינים אחרים ואנשים בכלל.

למרות שפניתי אל אלוהים לבקש מחילת חטאי והקדשתי את חיי ללכת אחריו, היו לי הרבה הרגלים ישנים של ייחוס לאחרים בדרכים שגויות שעדיין נדרשו לקדש. הדברים בבית המשיכו להשתפר אך עדיין היה מקום להתקדמות, מה שהוסיף למתח. ככל שעברו השנים, רמת המתח שלי המשיכה לעלות. לא ידעתי מה לעשות אתו, לכן פניתי לנטילת מינונים גבוהים של NoDoz® עם משקה אנרגיה לפני שהלכתי לישון, בניסיון להרגיע את עצבי כדי שאוכל להירדם (אל תנסו זאת בבית, זה מסוכן). למחרת הייתי קם ומתמודד עם הכל שוב. שנה שלמה רוב השנה נאבקתי במחשבות של אי רצון להמשיך בחיים. בזמן הזה היה לי חבר קרוב שנתן לי תמיכה רבה. אני מאמין שהמגע הקבוע שהיה לי עם חבר קרוב זה, התפילות של אחרים ונאמנותו של אלוהים שעבדו יחד מנעו ממני לעשות משהו שבו הייתי מתחרט לאחר מכן.

היה לי חבר קרוב אחר שעבר גם הוא הרבה אך נראה כי הוא מוצא את תשובות אלוהים למאבקי החיים. היינו יוצאים לארוחת ערב, מבלים יחד ומשוחחים על קשיי החיים. אני זוכר פעמים שבהן הייתי יורד מרכבו והדמעות זלגו על פניו כי הוא לא היה בטוח אם אצליח לעבור את זה. אחר כך הוא נסע למשימה בשדה למשך שנתיים כדי ללמד אנגלית.

אינני בטוח מה התרחש בחייו אך יום אחד קיבלנו ידיעה שהוא נעדר. לבסוף שמענו ממנו; הוא היה בסדר וחי שוב בארצות הברית. ליבי היה קרוע... אחד המעטים שהיו לי כחברים, עכשיו הפנה עורף למה שהוא פעם האמין בו ולמה שהוא פעם ניסה לשכנע אותי בו. ובכל זאת הנה אני, עדיין נאבק... מדוע לא פשוט לוותר על המאבק...? למה לא לחיות את החיים הקלים...? ככל שעבר הזמן, המשכתי לכמוה לאהבה ולקבלה. לפעמים המאבק, הכאב והכמיהה נראו כמעט בלתי נסבלים. אך ידעתי עמוק בפנים שויתור איננו מה שאני רוצה. זה לא יביא את התוצאה הסופית שאני רוצה. שוב באמצעות העידוד והמגע הקבוע עם חברי הקרוב, תפילות אחרים ונאמנותו של אלוהים, המשכתי לדחוף קדימה.

בחור צעיר אחר החל להתעניין בחיי ובסופו של דבר הפכנו לחברים קרובים. הוא ואשתו היו עידוד גדול עבורי. אז, בעקבות כמה חילוקי דעות עם הכנסייה, הם התסיסו ועזבו את הכנסייה. הם נשלכו הרבה ממה שעומד היה להם פעם. כך שוב מצאתי את עצמי עם חבר קרוב שהפנה עורף למה שבעבר עמד בשבילו. מה התועלת? מדוע החיים צריכים להיות כל כך קשים? אולי גם אני צריך להרים ידיים... אבל לא רציתי לזרוק לגמרי את אלוהים החוצה. אולי אוכל למצוא כנסייה פחות קפדנית. שוב הגעתי להכרה שזה לא באמת מה שאני רוצה. הכיוון הזה לא יקח אותי לאן שאני רוצה ללכת. אז שוב באמצעות העידוד והמגע הקבוע עם חברי הקרוב, תפילות אחרים ונאמנותו של אלוהים, המשכתי לדחוף קדימה. בזמנו זה היה קשה, אך כשאני מסתכל לאחור, אני רואה שלמדתי רבות מכל מה שעברתי.

בסתיו 2015 נסעתי למדינת וושינגטון בעקבות הזדמנות עבודה. כשהלכתי לשם, היו דברים שקורים בכנסיית הבית שהקשו עלי. בגלל כל הלחץ שעמד בפניי, הרגשתי מיואש לגבי חיי הכנסייה, הנצרות וחיים בכלל. לא רציתי לנטוש את הנצרות שלי, אך תהיתי, "האם זה באמת מה שכולו קשור?" "מדוע אנשים פשוט לא יכולים להסתדר?" האם זה באמת מה שאלוהים חשב בעבור עמו? אם אנו "משיחים קטנים" כפי שאנו טוענים להיות, האם לא היינו צריכים לדעת להסתדר? האם לא היינו צריכים להיות אלו ששמחים ומלאי חיים?

נסעתי לוושינגטון עם מחשבות כאלה בראשי. בזמן שהייתי שם, נכחתי בכנסייה שהייתה גם מקראית וגם רוחנית. קשה לתאר את כל מה שקרה במוחי, בלבי ובחיי במהלך ששת החודשים ההם. אך עזבתי משם וחזרתי הביתה עם כוח וחזון מחודשים.

עלינו להיות אור העולם! עלינו להיות בעלי מה להציע לאחרים! עלינו לדעת להסתדר בינינו! כן, אנו עוברים זמנים קשים באופן אישי ובאופן קולקטיבי ככנסייה, אך אם נלחם את המאבק הטוב של האמונה, אם נסיים את דרכנו, אם נשמור את האמונה, מונחת לנו לכל אחד צְרָת צִדְקָה—כתר של צְּדָקָה, אשר ייתן לי אדון, השופט הצדיק, ביום ההוא: ולא רק לי, אלא גם לכל אלה שאוהבים את הופעתו. נלחמתי את המאבק הטוב, סיימתי את מסלולי, שמרתי את האמונה: מעתה מורחב לי כתר של צְדָקָה, אשר ייתן לי האדון, השופט הצדיק, ביום ההוא: ולא רק לי, אלא גם לכל אלה שאוהבים את הופעתו –2 טימותיוס 4:7-8.

15 ביוני 2018, בשעה 16:40. צריחת המנסר של שירותי החירום חתכה את אחר הצהריים השקט כשהיא קרקלה לחיים. "התהפכות רכב יחיד ברחוב 'גינגקו', אפשרי לכידה," היה הפרסום שחזר. כשנכנסנו לזירה, ישבה שם צעירה שנראתה באמצע העשרים לחייה והייתה חבולה בגלוי. עם דם ודמעות זורמים על פניה, חזרה על המשפטים הללו, "אני לא רוצה למות... אני לא מוכנה למות... אולי אני לא אראה יותר את התינוק שלי." כששניות הפכו לדקות, החובשים ניסו להרגיע את עצביה החרדתיים. חיפשנו ברכב המעוך ובאזור הסמוך אחר התינוק החסר לכאורה. כל הזמן היא ישבה שם עם קמטי דאגה ופחד. דמעות ודם זלגו על פניה, והיא חזרה על, "אולי אני לא אראה את התינוק שלי יותר... אני לא רוצה למות... אני לא מוכנה למות."

כמגיבים ראשונים, כל מה שמצאנו היה כיסא רכב שלא הותקן כראוי, ללא ראיה לתינוק בכל מקום. כשהצוות האמבולנס קשור אותה על הסלאינג והעמיסוה באמבולנס, היא עדיין חזרה על, "איפה התינוק שלי...? אני לא מוכנה למות... אני לא רוצה למות... אולי אני לא אראה את התינוק שלי יותר."

כשהעזבתי את הזירה באותו ערב, עם התמונה והביטויים האלה רצות במוחי, נחתו עלי שתי מחשבות רציניות. אם זה הייתי אני, ששרדתי בדרך נס תאונה וישבתי שם לצד רכבי, בקושי צלול, עם דם זורם על פניי, מה הייתי אומר? במה ייזכרו החובשים וצוות החילוץ ממני? האם הייתי מוכן למות? האם הייתי ברור מול ה'?

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

כנוצרים, מתי בפעם האחרונה עזרנו למישהו להכין את נפשו למות? כמאמינים שנגאלו מהאסון ומהכאוס של חיי חטא (ראו 1 קורינתים 6:9-11), עלינו …להיות תמיד מוכנים לתת תשובה לכל אדם המבקש מכם סיבת התקוה שבתוככם בענווה ויראת כבוד: –1 פטרוס 3:15.

בסתיו 2018, אלוהים פתח בפני דלת עבורי לעבור לכנסייה במדינה אחרת שבה מצאתי יציבות. כאן הביא אלוהים בחורה אדוקה לחיי, ונשאנו ב-30 בנובמבר 2019. הנישואים והאחים שסבבו אותי עם חניכה, רחמנות ותמיכה בתפילה עזרו לי לגדול באדון במישורים רבים.

השהות כאן עוררה בי חזון מחודש להיות אור העולם. היום אני מודה שאלוהים לא הניח לי ללכת. ככל שהמשכתי להיאבק במלחמה הרוחנית, אלוהים המשיך לתת לי כוח וחכמה לעשות את הדבר הנכון הבא. עם כל ניצחון, כוחי הלך והתחזק. התקרבו אל אלוהים, והוא יתקדם אליכם... –יעקב 4:8. אני מודה לאלוהים שנתן לי נצחון ולעזור לי למצוא את מקור האהבה, הביטחון והמטרה הסופיים שלי — אדוני ומושיעי, ישוע המשיח.

The year was around 60 AD. The Apostle Paul had been apprehended and almost killed in the Temple at Jerusalem by a mob of angry Jews.

A few days later, he had been whisked off to the Roman Procurator Felix because of danger from a group of Jewish plotters. Felix had heard his case and though there was no evidence to convict Paul, Felix had kept him in prison for the next two years until the new Procurator, Festus, took his place.

King Herod Agrippa II came to visit Festus and the two of them listened to Paul speak. During the hearing Paul …reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, [until finally] Felix trembled, and answered, Go thy way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for thee –Acts 24:25. Then towards the end of Paul’s oration …Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad –Acts 26:24.

Festus was not speaking of scientific knowledge, but of the fact that Paul was well-studied. Worse yet, Paul was making the governor uncomfortable with his sinful life and his reasoning made clear that the only solution for both Festus and Agrippa was to follow the Scriptures of the Hebrews.

Paul was well educated. He made clear in his letters and sermons, quoting not only from the Jewish Bible, but also from a variety of Greek and Cretan philosophers and poets.

In more modern times, it seems as though science is not a friend to faith. Many scientists claim that the idea of an intelligent designer of the Universe is ludicrous. Further, many of them would say that those who believe such things are the next thing to savages.

It certainly turns many Christians away from science entirely. They do not see something so antagonistic to the fundamental Christian faith as being useful.

I can understand this point of view, but I think that we should not give up learning simply because some of those who claim to be so knowledgeable are, in actuality, quite foolish.

Creation

When I think about the subject of science, I often begin with the subject of creation. This is the beginning of everything and is the first place where “science” and the Bible first come into conflict.

Science is simply unable to accept that there could have been a Creator God who set in motion everything that we see.

There are many books delving into the subject of intelligent design and seeing God’s fingerprints throughout creation. It takes a lot more faith to believe that the universe happened by chance, than to believe in a Creator.

The Bible makes it clear that God was not only present at the time of Creation, but it was also He who began it (John 1:1-3). Paul says For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse –Romans 1:20.

People should be able to discern that there is a Creator God involved in our world and the universe from the time of Creation. They should be able to understand a few other things about Him as well. Perhaps most important for our discussion here, we can tell by looking at creation that God is an orderly God and that He created the world to function with a specific structure and laws that govern it.

This is one of the big differences between the Creation account found in Genesis and the myths of creation found in other cultures of the time. The Bible makes it clear that God intentionally created the world, that He did so in an orderly fashion, and that He made certain that every part of it meshed with all the other parts. There is no magic or mystical thinking in the Genesis account.

The Laws of the Universe Still Stand

There are many people who believe that they can alter the way that the universe functions, that they can behave in immoral ways and not suffer the rewards of sin, and that they can do foolish things and not suffer the consequences of their behavior.

The Prophet Jeremiah tells us that there are laws which are in place that will not cease to function. Thus saith the LORD, which giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night, which divideth the sea when the waves thereof roar; The LORD of hosts is his name: If those ordinances depart from before me, saith the LORD, then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before me for ever –Jeremiah 31:35-36.

There is a whole set of laws that governs the way that the earth rotates on its axis and orbits the sun. Everything from the speed of light to the way that gravity pulls things towards large bodies of mass was instituted at the time of Creation—…all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation –2 Peter 3:4.

Since those laws continue and do not fluctuate, we are able to understand them—at least in part. This is what science is—the study of the natural world that we see and an attempt to comprehend the ways in which it works. God created our world in such a way that if you do an experiment the same way every time, you will get the same results every time.

Science Will Never Understand Everything

The Prophet Isaiah says, For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the LORD. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts –Isaiah 55:8-9.

Even the smartest quantum physicists will admit that they don’t understand everything. In fact, the number of questions that they have is greater than the whole storehouse of knowledge that has been accumulated.

Most of us will have far less understanding of the universe than that. We won’t understand all the details of how the atom functions. We won’t be able to do the calculus necessary to put a satellite into orbit. That’s all right. The important thing is that we learn what we can in order to understand what an amazing and orderly God we serve.

Presuppositions are a Problem

The biggest problem that we see in science is not the science itself, rather it is the biases of the people performing the science. The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God… –Psalm 14:1. By this definition, many scientists are fools.

I don’t say this lightly. Atheists observe the universe and since they believe that there cannot be a God, they must then explain how it exists without the presence of an actual Creator. This is the heart of foolishness.

When they come to gaps in their knowledge, they are silent and yet the Christian can explain them in a few simple words. As I said before, when we look at the complexity of the universe, from the tiniest things to the largest galaxies, we can see the hands of God at work.

When I consider thy heavens, the work of thy fingers, the moon and the stars, which thou hast ordained; What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of man, that thou visitest him? –Psalm 8:3-4. When we think about the world around us, when we read what scientists write, it is crucial that we come to it with a knowledge that God is behind all of this. For in him we live, and move, and have our being… – Acts 17:28, and nothing that science can discern will change that.

Science should be like a detective, uncovering God’s fingerprints on the universe, not someone bound and determined to discredit His very real presence.

Many Scientists Believe in God

Looking into the past, many scientists were men who believed in the God of the Bible. Isaac Newton, Francis Bacon, Nicholas Copernicus and many others believed in the Bible and were forthright in their expression of this faith to others.

In more modern days, there are many men and women of science who believe in the God of the Bible. Just because one is working in science doesn’t mean that they are unable to have a life of faith.

Many people have co-opted scientific discoveries to push messages that are against Christian belief and teaching.

We need to remember that when there is a set of facts, there are usually different explanations that can account for their presence. Creation and evolution examine the same facts of nature, yet from a different perspective or bias, thus they end up with vastly different conclusions. Perhaps it is a little like a Sherlock Holmes story, where Dr. Watson routinely takes the facts and gives an inaccurate explanation of them, while the detective takes the same information and gives the right explanation.

Science and Medicine

It is not against Scripture to research how things work in our universe, as long as we do so within a Biblical framework and understanding that there is a Creator God who is ordering it all.

Modern medicine is an application of many various fields, including anatomy, microanatomy, genetics, and biochemistry. The point, in this case, is to observe the human body the best that we can and then to fix the things that go wrong with it. Doctors can be scientists, but most of them are simply applying knowledge which has been passed down to them through their training.

Observation is where things start. Let’s consider diabetes as an example. Aretaeus of Cappadocia in the second century AD was the first person to give a complete description of diabetes and actually gave the disease the name diabetes. The problem was that while he was able to diagnose people with this illness, he had no treatment to help his patients. Observation had only taken him so far.

Over time, other work was done that demonstrated that the problem was an issue in the pancreas and that something was specifically wrong with the islet cells. Even into the early 1900s, there was no cure for Diabetes Mellitus and the only solution that doctors had to offer was an extremely low glycemic diet with severe calorie limits—attempting to keep patients at 500 or 600 calories a day. As can be imagined, this wasn’t an ideal treatment.

It wasn’t until the 1920s that a couple of researchers in Canada discovered a way to extract insulin from dogs and administered it to a 14-year-old who was dying of diabetes. The extract saved his life and began a new era for people with diabetes.

This is the way that things work. We begin by observing a disease and various medications that seem to be effective for it, then over time and through meticulous testing we can assess what treatments are most effective for that illness.

Studies in which half of the participants with a disease are given a medication or treatment and half are given a placebo (a pill without medical efficacy) are still the most effective way of telling whether something really works.

Why Treatments Need to be Studied

There is a real tendency to believe that the things that you have been taught are effective. We know that George Washington died of pneumonia. His doctors probably damaged his chances of recovery by bleeding him four times for a total of close to 40 percent of his blood volume. They probably would have bled him a fifth time, but he wasn’t thought to be strong enough to survive the procedure.

Doctors bled patients because they believed that there were toxic build ups in the blood stream that had to be let out. Most of the people who died after bloodletting would probably have died anyway, but bleeding people who are really sick certainly doesn’t help them recover.

Maybe the doctors simply wanted to be doing something. Patients expected bloodletting and so they met those expectations, even though it harmed the patients.

Experience is what lets you make the same mistakes with a lot more confidence.

What Makes a Good Study

Good studies—have plenty of patients in them, have a control group (that either receives an inactive pill called a placebo, or the current best treatment for that disease), and have the test group getting the new treatment. It is also important for the control group and the test group to be matched as closely as possible. Finally, the size of the groups in the study is vital to the conclusions of the study. If there are only ten or twenty patients in the study, it is not a large enough group to really sort out if something works or doesn’t.

For many diseases there is something called a placebo effect. This placebo effect is when people get better from an illness even though they are not receiving something that should be effective at treating the malady. Interestingly, in studies, many people get side effects from the inert pills. If 20 percent of the people getting the placebo get better and 45 percent of the people getting the treatment get better, that would indicate that the treatment is effective. If the difference is minimal—say 20 percent of the placebo group and 23 percent of the treatment group improve—then the treatment isn’t effective.

Problems

The biggest problem with many treatments is that they simply aren’t studied. Vitamin supplements and herbal compounds may work, but many of them have never actually been studied in a trial comparing them with a control group. Most of the information is anecdotal. The fact that someone’s grandmother or uncle benefited from something is possibly an indication that it is effective, but it doesn’t tell us how effective this treatment is or what dosage level is ideal.

Another issue is when studies simply don’t have enough participants to really give accurate information. Many studies only include ten or twenty patients. That is simply not enough to identify how well a treatment works or what side effects can be expected. For a drug to be approved by the FDA, it will typically have been studied on between 1,000 to 3,000 patients with the disease.

A final issue with studies is when they show that a medication is effective, but the effect isn’t clinically significant. As an example, a new injectable medication for dementia (aducanumab) was recently approved by the FDA. It is very expensive, and the benefit seemed to be small. Patients who were on it got an average of 1.5 more test questions right on an 85-question mental status questionnaire after 18 months compared to the control group.

One can rightly question if the benefits shown by this medication are worth the 50,000 dollar-per-year cost. More than that, how much of a meaningful improvement in someone’s everyday activities would come from using such a medicine? It seems unlikely that it would make very much of a difference.

It is unfortunate, but drug companies will always try to make it seem like their medicine is the best, even if the studies do not show significant benefit over existing, cheaper options.

Conclusion

Christians are faced with a world which does not love them or their beliefs. Many would try to use science as a way to bludgeon them into giving up their faith. I hope that does not lead us to give up on the scientific method or to give up attempting to understand the laws behind the universe that God created.

The scientific method is valid, even if many of the people who use it are atheists or agnostics. If a treatment works, it should be observable, testable, and repeatable.

Even as we approach it, we have a basic understanding of the universe that atheists don’t have. Knowing that there is a Creator God who loves us makes a major difference as we interpret the results of all the different observations that are being made in the fields of medicine and other places.

Those who do not know God are bound to be ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth –2 Timothy 3:7. On the other hand, if we begin with a Biblical understanding, we can use science as a tool to help us to understand the creation that He has placed around us.

Tahunnya kira-kira 60 M. Rasul Paulus telah ditangkap dan nyaris dibunuh di Bait Allah di Yerusalem oleh massa orang Yahudi yang marah.

Beberapa hari kemudian, ia dibawa kepada Pemerintah Romawi, Feliks, karena adanya bahaya dari sekelompok perencana Yahudi. Feliks mendengar kasusnya dan meskipun tidak ada bukti untuk menghukum Paulus, Feliks menahannya di penjara selama dua tahun berikutnya sampai Pemerintah yang baru, Festus, menggantikannya.

Raja Herodes Agripa II datang mengunjungi Festus dan keduanya mendengarkan Paulus berbicara. Selama sidang Paulus …berkata tentang kebenaran, tentang pengendalian diri, dan tentang penghakiman yang akan datang, [sampai akhirnya] Feliks gemetar, dan menjawab: Pergilah untuk sekarang; apabila ada kesempatan yang tepat, aku akan memanggil engkau –Kisah Para Rasul 24:25. Lalu menjelang akhir pidato Paulus …Festus berseru dengan suara nyaring: Paulus, engkau kecewa; banyaknya pelajaran membuat engkau gila –Kisah Para Rasul 26:24.

Festus tidak berbicara tentang pengetahuan ilmiah, melainkan tentang kenyataan bahwa Paulus banyak belajar. Lebih parah lagi, Paulus membuat sang gubernur tidak nyaman dengan kehidupan berdosanya dan alasan Paulus menjelaskan bahwa satu-satunya solusi bagi Festus dan Agripa adalah mengikuti Kitab Suci orang Yahudi.

Paulus berpendidikan baik. Ia menegaskan dalam surat-surat dan khotbahnya, mengutip tidak hanya dari Alkitab Yahudi, tetapi juga dari berbagai filsuf dan penyair Yunani serta Kret.

Dalam zaman yang lebih modern, seolah-olah ilmu pengetahuan tidak bersahabat dengan iman. Banyak ilmuwan mengklaim bahwa gagasan tentang perancang cerdas alam semesta adalah konyol. Selain itu, banyak dari mereka akan mengatakan bahwa orang-orang yang percaya demikian hampir sejajar dengan orang yang primitif.

Tentu saja hal itu membuat banyak orang Kristen menjauhi ilmu pengetahuan sepenuhnya. Mereka tidak melihat sesuatu yang begitu bertentangan dengan iman Kristen pokok sebagai sesuatu yang berguna.

Saya dapat memahami sudut pandang ini, tetapi saya pikir kita tidak boleh menyerah belajar hanya karena beberapa orang yang mengaku berpengetahuan ternyata, pada kenyataannya, cukup bodoh.

Penciptaan

Saat saya memikirkan subjek ilmu pengetahuan, saya sering memulai dengan topik penciptaan. Ini adalah awal dari segala sesuatu dan merupakan tempat pertama di mana “ilmupengetahuan” dan Alkitab bersinggungan.

Ilmu pengetahuan tidak dapat menerima bahwa bisa ada Allah Pencipta yang menggerakkan segala yang kita lihat.

Ada banyak buku yang membahas tentang perancangan cerdas dan melihat jejak Tuhan di seluruh ciptaan. Dibutuhkan jauh lebih banyak iman untuk percaya bahwa alam semesta terjadi begitu saja karena kebetulan, dibandingkan dengan mempercayai adanya Sang Pencipta.

Alkitab menjelaskan bahwa Allah tidak hanya hadir pada saat Penciptaan, tetapi Dialah yang memulainya (Yohanes 1:1-3). Paulus berkata Karena apa yang dapat dikenal tentang Allah adalah nyata bagi mereka. Allah telah menyatakannya kepada mereka. Dari penciptaan dunia kaitkan-Nya dengan segala sesuatu yang terlihat—kekuatan-Nya yang kekal dan keilahian-Nya—sehingga mereka tidak dapat berdalih. –Roma 1:20.

Orang seharusnya dapat membedakan bahwa ada Allah Pencipta yang terlibat dalam dunia kita dan alam semesta sejak saat Penciptaan. Mereka juga seharusnya dapat memahami beberapa hal lain tentang Dia. Mungkin yang paling penting untuk pembahasan kita di sini, kita dapat melihat dari ciptaan bahwa Allah adalah Allah yang teratur dan bahwa Dia menciptakan dunia agar berfungsi dengan struktur dan hukum tertentu yang mengaturnya.

Ini adalah salah satu perbedaan besar antara kisah Penciptaan yang terdapat di Kejadian dan mitos penciptaan yang ditemukan di budaya lain pada masa itu. Alkitab menegaskan bahwa Allah secara sengaja menciptakan dunia, bahwa Dia melakukannya secara teratur, dan bahwa Dia memastikan setiap bagian saling berhubungan dengan bagian lainnya. Tidak ada unsur magis atau pemikiran mistis dalam kisah Kejadian.

Hukum-hukum Alam Semesta Tetap Berlaku

Ada banyak orang yang percaya bahwa mereka dapat mengubah cara kerja alam semesta, bahwa mereka dapat berperilaku amoral tanpa menanggung akibat dosa, dan bahwa mereka dapat melakukan hal-hal bodoh tanpa menanggung konsekuensi dari perilaku mereka.

Nabi Yeremia memberitahu kita bahwa ada hukum-hukum yang berlaku yang tidak akan berhenti berfungsi. Beginilah firman TUHAN, yang menjadikan matahari sebagai terang pada siang hari, dan peraturan-peraturan bulan dan bintang-bintang sebagai terang pada malam hari, yang membagi laut apabila gelombangnya bergemuruh; nama-Nya TUHAN semesta alam: Jika peraturan-peraturan itu berpaling dari depan-Ku—demikianlah firman TUHAN—maka juga umat Israel akan terputus sebagai bangsa dari hadapan-Ku untuk selama-lamanya. –Yeremia 31:35-36.

Ada satu set hukum yang mengatur cara bumi berputar pada porosnya dan mengorbit matahari. Segala sesuatu dari kecepatan cahaya hingga cara gravitasi menarik benda menuju massa besar diinstitusikan pada saat Penciptaan—…segala sesuatu tetap seperti semula sejak permulaan penciptaan—2 Petrus 3:4.

Karena hukum-hukum itu berlanjut dan tidak berfluktuasi, kita mampu memahaminya—setidaknya sebagian. Inilah yang disebut ilmu pengetahuan—studi tentang dunia alam yang kita lihat dan upaya untuk memahami cara kerjanya. Allah menciptakan dunia kita sedemikian rupa sehingga jika Anda melakukan sebuah percobaan dengan cara yang sama berulang kali, Anda akan mendapatkan hasil yang sama setiap kali.

Ilmu Pengetahuan Tidak Akan Pernah Memahami Segalanya

Nabi Yesaya berkata, Sebab rancangan-Ku bukan seperti rancanganmu, dan jalanmu bukan seperti jalan-Ku—demikianlah firman TUHAN. Karena setinggi langit dari pada bumi, demikianlah jalan-Ku lebih tinggi dari jalanmu dan rancangan-Ku lebih tinggi dari rancanganmu. –Yesaya 55:8-9.

Bahkan fisikawan kuantum yang paling pintar pun akan mengakui bahwa mereka tidak memahami segalanya. Bahkan jumlah pertanyaan yang mereka miliki lebih besar daripada seluruh gudang pengetahuan yang telah terkumpul.

Kebanyakan dari kita akan memiliki pemahaman tentang alam semesta yang jauh lebih sedikit daripada itu. Kita tidak akan memahami semua detail tentang bagaimana atom berfungsi. Kita tidak akan mampu melakukan kalkulus yang diperlukan untuk menempatkan satelit ke orbit. Tidak apa-apa. Hal penting adalah bahwa kita mempelajari apa yang bisa kita pelajari untuk memahami betapa menakjubkan dan teraturnya Allah yang kita layani.

Presuposisi adalah Masalah

Masalah terbesar yang kita lihat dalam ilmu pengetahuan bukanlah ilmu pengetahuan itu sendiri, melainkan bias dari orang yang melakukan ilmu pengetahuan. Orang bebal berkata dalam hatinya: Tidak ada Allah… –Mazmur 14:1. Menurut definisi ini, banyak ilmuwan adalah orang bodoh.

Saya tidak mengatakan ini dengan enteng. Orang-orang atheis mengamati alam semesta dan karena mereka percaya bahwa tidak mungkin ada Allah, mereka harus menjelaskan bagaimana alam semesta ada tanpa adanya Sang Pencipta yang sebenarnya. Inilah inti kebodohan.

Ketika mereka menemui celah dalam pengetahuan mereka, mereka tetap diam sementara orang Kristen dapat menjelaskannya dengan beberapa kata sederhana. Seperti yang saya katakan sebelumnya, ketika kita melihat kompleksitas alam semesta, dari hal-hal yang paling kecil hingga galaksi terbesar, kita dapat melihat tangan Allah bekerja.

Ketika aku memandang langit-Mu, buatan jari-jari-Mu, bulan dan bintang yang Kaaturkan, apakah manusia sehingga Engkau mengingatnya? Apakah anak manusia sehingga Engkau memedulikan dia? –Mazmur 8:3-4. Ketika kita merenungkan dunia di sekitar kita, ketika kita membaca apa yang ditulis para ilmuwan, sangat penting bahwa kita mendekatinya dengan pengetahuan bahwa Allah ada di balik semua ini. Karena di dalam Dia kita hidup, bergerak dan ada… –Kisah Para Rasul 17:28, dan tidak ada yang dapat diungkap ilmu pengetahuan yang akan mengubah itu.

Ilmu pengetahuan seharusnya seperti seorang detektif, mengungkap jejak tangan Allah pada alam semesta, bukan seseorang yang bertekad untuk mendiskreditkan kehadiran-Nya yang nyata.

Banyak Ilmuwan Percaya kepada Allah

Melihat ke masa lalu, banyak ilmuwan adalah orang-orang yang percaya kepada Allah Alkitab. Isaac Newton, Francis Bacon, Nicholas Copernicus dan banyak lainnya percaya kepada Alkitab dan terang-terangan menyatakan iman ini kepada orang lain.

Pada masa modern, ada banyak pria dan wanita ilmuwan yang percaya kepada Allah Alkitab. Hanya karena seseorang bekerja di bidang ilmu pengetahuan tidak berarti mereka tidak mampu memiliki kehidupan iman.

Banyak orang telah menggunakan penemuan ilmiah untuk mendorong pesan-pesan yang bertentangan dengan kepercayaan dan pengajaran Kristen.

Kita perlu mengingat bahwa ketika ada seperangkat fakta, biasanya ada berbagai penjelasan yang dapat menjelaskan keberadaan fakta-fakta tersebut. Penciptaan dan evolusi memeriksa fakta-fakta alam yang sama, tetapi dari perspektif atau bias yang berbeda, sehingga mereka berujung pada kesimpulan yang sangat berbeda. Mungkin sedikit seperti cerita Sherlock Holmes, di mana Dr. Watson secara rutin mengambil fakta dan memberikan penjelasan yang tidak akurat, sementara sang detektif mengambil informasi yang sama dan memberikan penjelasan yang benar.

Ilmu Pengetahuan dan Kedokteran

Tidak bertentangan dengan Kitab Suci untuk meneliti bagaimana segala sesuatu bekerja di alam semesta kita, selama kita melakukannya dalam kerangka dan pemahaman Alkitab bahwa ada Allah Pencipta yang mengaturnya semua.

Kedokteran modern adalah penerapan dari berbagai bidang, termasuk anatomi, mikroanatomi, genetika, dan biokimia. Tujuannya, dalam hal ini, adalah mengamati tubuh manusia sebaik mungkin dan kemudian memperbaiki hal-hal yang salah dengannya. Dokter bisa menjadi ilmuwan, tetapi kebanyakan dari mereka hanya menerapkan pengetahuan yang diwariskan kepada mereka melalui pelatihan.

Pengamatan adalah tempat segala sesuatu dimulai. Mari kita pertimbangkan diabetes sebagai contoh. Areteus dari Kappadokia pada abad kedua M adalah orang pertama yang memberi deskripsi lengkap tentang diabetes dan sebenarnya memberikan penyakit itu nama diabetes. Masalahnya adalah meskipun ia mampu mendiagnosis orang dengan penyakit ini, ia tidak memiliki pengobatan untuk membantu pasiennya. Pengamatan hanya membawanya sejauh itu.

Seiring waktu, pekerjaan lain dilakukan yang menunjukkan bahwa masalah itu berasal dari pankreas dan bahwa ada sesuatu yang secara khusus salah dengan sel-sel pulau pankreas. Bahkan hingga awal 1900-an, belum ada obat untuk Diabetes Mellitus dan satu-satunya solusi yang ditawarkan dokter adalah diet glikemik sangat rendah dengan batasan kalori yang ketat—berusaha menjaga pasien pada 500 atau 600 kalori per hari. Seperti yang dapat dibayangkan, ini bukanlah pengobatan yang ideal.

Baru pada tahun 1920-an beberapa peneliti di Kanada menemukan cara mengekstrak insulin dari anjing dan memberikannya kepada seorang bocah 14 tahun yang sekarat karena diabetes. Ekstrak itu menyelamatkan nyawanya dan memulai era baru bagi penderita diabetes.

Beginilah cara kerja segala sesuatu. Kita mulai dengan mengamati suatu penyakit dan berbagai obat yang tampak efektif untuknya, lalu seiring waktu dan melalui pengujian teliti kita dapat menilai pengobatan mana yang paling efektif untuk penyakit itu.

Studi di mana setengah dari peserta yang sakit diberi obat atau perawatan dan setengah lagi diberi plasebo (pil tanpa khasiat medis) masih merupakan cara paling efektif untuk mengetahui apakah sesuatu benar-benar bekerja.

Mengapa Perawatan Perlu Dipelajari

Ada kecenderungan nyata untuk percaya bahwa hal-hal yang telah diajarkan kepada Anda itu efektif. Kita tahu bahwa George Washington meninggal karena pneumonia. Dokternya mungkin merusak peluang kesembuhannya dengan mengeluarkan darahnya empat kali sehingga hampir mencapai 40 persen dari volume darahnya. Mungkin mereka akan mengeluarkan darahnya untuk kali kelima, tetapi ia dianggap tidak cukup kuat untuk bertahan dari prosedur itu.

Dokter mengeluarkan darah pasien karena mereka percaya bahwa ada penumpukan racun dalam aliran darah yang harus dikeluarkan. Kebanyakan orang yang meninggal setelah pengeluaran darah mungkin memang akan meninggal juga, tetapi mengeluarkan darah orang yang sangat sakit tentu tidak membantu mereka pulih.

Mungkin para dokter hanya ingin melakukan sesuatu. Pasien mengharapkan pengeluaran darah dan sehingga harapan itu dipenuhi, meskipun hal itu membahayakan pasien.

Pengalaman adalah apa yang membuat Anda membuat kesalahan yang sama dengan jauh lebih percaya diri.

Apa yang Membuat Suatu Studi Baik

Studi yang baik—memiliki banyak pasien di dalamnya, memiliki kelompok kontrol (yang menerima pil tidak aktif yang disebut plasebo, atau pengobatan terbaik yang ada untuk penyakit itu), dan memiliki kelompok uji yang menerima pengobatan baru. Penting juga agar kelompok kontrol dan kelompok uji dicocokkan sedekat mungkin. Akhirnya, ukuran kelompok dalam studi sangat penting untuk kesimpulan studi. Jika hanya ada sepuluh atau dua puluh pasien dalam studi, itu tidak cukup besar untuk benar-benar menentukan apakah sesuatu bekerja atau tidak.

Untuk banyak penyakit ada sesuatu yang disebut efek plasebo. Efek plasebo ini terjadi ketika orang menjadi lebih baik dari suatu penyakit meskipun mereka tidak menerima sesuatu yang seharusnya efektif dalam mengobati penyakit tersebut. Menariknya, dalam studi, banyak orang mengalami efek samping dari pil inert tersebut. Jika 20 persen orang yang menerima plasebo menjadi lebih baik dan 45 persen orang yang menerima pengobatan menjadi lebih baik, itu menunjukkan bahwa pengobatan itu efektif. Jika perbedaannya minimal—katakanlah 20 persen dari kelompok plasebo dan 23 persen dari kelompok pengobatan membaik—maka pengobatan itu tidak efektif.

Masalah

Masalah terbesar dengan banyak pengobatan adalah bahwa mereka tidak pernah dipelajari. Suplemen vitamin dan senyawa herbal mungkin bekerja, tetapi banyak dari mereka tidak pernah benar-benar dipelajari dalam uji yang membandingkannya dengan kelompok kontrol. Sebagian besar informasinya bersifat anekdot. Fakta bahwa nenek atau paman seseorang mendapat manfaat dari sesuatu mungkin menunjukkan bahwa itu efektif, tetapi itu tidak memberi tahu kita seberapa efektif pengobatan ini atau berapa dosis yang ideal.

Masalah lain adalah ketika studi tidak memiliki cukup peserta untuk benar-benar memberikan informasi yang akurat. Banyak studi hanya melibatkan sepuluh atau dua puluh pasien. Itu jelas tidak cukup untuk mengidentifikasi seberapa baik suatu pengobatan bekerja atau efek samping apa yang dapat diharapkan. Agar suatu obat disetujui oleh FDA, biasanya obat itu telah dipelajari pada antara 1.000 hingga 3.000 pasien yang menderita penyakit tersebut.

Masalah terakhir dengan studi adalah ketika mereka menunjukkan bahwa suatu obat efektif, tetapi efeknya tidak signifikan secara klinis. Sebagai contoh, obat suntik baru untuk demensia (aducanumab) baru-baru ini disetujui oleh FDA. Harganya sangat mahal, dan manfaatnya tampak kecil. Pasien yang menggunakannya memperoleh rata-rata 1,5 pertanyaan lagi yang benar pada kuesioner status mental 85-pertanyaan setelah 18 bulan dibandingkan kelompok kontrol.

Orang berhak mempertanyakan apakah manfaat yang ditunjukkan oleh obat ini sepadan dengan biaya 50.000 dolar per tahun. Lebih dari itu, seberapa besar peningkatan bermakna dalam aktivitas sehari-hari seseorang yang akan diperoleh dari menggunakan obat semacam itu? Tampaknya tidak mungkin bahwa hal itu akan membuat perbedaan besar.

Sungguh disayangkan, tetapi perusahaan farmasi akan selalu berusaha membuat obat mereka tampak yang terbaik, bahkan jika studi tidak menunjukkan manfaat signifikan dibandingkan pilihan yang lebih murah dan sudah ada.

Kesimpulan

Orang Kristen dihadapkan pada dunia yang tidak mencintai mereka atau kepercayaan mereka. Banyak yang akan mencoba menggunakan ilmu pengetahuan sebagai alat untuk memukul mereka agar menyerah dari iman mereka. Saya berharap itu tidak membuat kita menyerah pada metode ilmiah atau menyerah mencoba memahami hukum-hukum di balik alam semesta yang diciptakan Allah.

Metode ilmiah itu sah, meskipun banyak orang yang menggunakannya adalah atheis atau agnostik. Jika suatu perawatan bekerja, itu harus dapat diamati, dapat diuji, dan dapat diulang.

Bahkan ketika kita mendekatinya, kita memiliki pemahaman dasar tentang alam semesta yang tidak dimiliki orang atheis. Mengetahui bahwa ada Allah Pencipta yang mengasihi kita membuat perbedaan besar ketika kita menafsirkan hasil dari berbagai pengamatan yang dibuat di bidang kedokteran dan tempat-tempat lain.

Mereka yang tidak mengenal Allah pasti akan selalu belajar dan tidak pernah mencapai pengetahuan kebenaran –2 Timotius 3:7. Di sisi lain, jika kita memulai dengan pemahaman Alkitabiah, kita dapat menggunakan ilmu pengetahuan sebagai alat untuk membantu kita memahami ciptaan yang Dia tempatkan di sekitar kita.

I grew up in the same church setting in which my parents were born and raised. However, by the time I was 10, my parents began to be concerned with the direction the young folks were going and wanted something different for their children. So, my parents got in touch with a church from another state, which helped them make connections with a small church that was located close to where we lived.

I was more of a quiet, strong-willed child and was quickly turning into a rebellious teenager. My parents did all they knew to do with me at the time. One of which was making the move to this new church since it had more of a godly youth environment. I had a hard time with this change. At our old church, I had friends that were on the same page as me and supported me in my rebellious ways, but at the new church I was more of the “bad guy” and didn’t fit in with the other young people.

Over the course of time that church dissolved, and my parents decided to move to another state, closer to a more stable church. So it was, that, when I was 14, we spent our first night in a different state, in a different house, on a different road, and with different neighbors. We went shopping in a different town and went to a different church, with people that I barely knew. I didn’t like change. I found it challenging to meet new people and make new friends. I struggled majorly with all these changes, so, I never bothered trying to plug in and be an active part in our new life. Instead, I slowly built walls around my life and heart, all the while growing colder and more rebellious.

As I grew older and harder, my parents tried to work with me, but I would have nothing to do with it. I eventually got a job and was introduced to country music and other worldly things. Since I enjoy work, I poured myself into it and worked long hours. That way I wouldn’t need to be around the family or church people, and I wouldn’t need to go to church activities. Thus, I became more removed and isolated from those around me.

The church people didn’t know how to relate to me; most of them just left me to myself. Deep down I was desperately longing for love and acceptance from my family and church. This caused me to spiral downward. I continued to stuff my feelings and build a wall around myself, all the while hardening my heart further. As time went on, I withdrew more and more from my family and the church. I felt more and more like a social misfit that no one knew what to do with. I decided I was going to run away and live my own life.

Somehow my parents got wind of this idea and tried to do all that they knew to do to help me, but I resented it. Looking back, I know without a doubt that they were doing it out of love and care, but there was a great lack in our relationship. Thus, I continued to grow harder and colder.

The summer I was 17, a visiting minister (‘Mike’) and his family came to our church for meetings. I knew them from years before and somehow through our interaction during the meetings my heart started to soften and open. I’m not quite sure why, but for some reason, I decided that I wanted to go spend the winter with them. So, my parents got in contact with them, and it was decided that I could stay with them for a few months.

My plan was to spend a few months away from everything and then I would return home when I was almost 18. Once I was 18, I was planning to leave home and do my own thing. I was certain no one could stop me because I would be of legal age. However, God obviously had different plans...

Somehow ‘Mike’ convinced me to go to along to a week of meetings in another state. While we were there, I don’t remember that the conviction was any stronger than any other time. However, one evening after the service he asked me if I wanted to become a Christian and have my sins forgiven. I don’t remember what I told him, but we talked for a while. He took me through the Bible, helping me to see what God says about it all; then we prayed. When we got up from praying, I can’t say that something major happened, but it was definitely the night that I found salvation! That night, something changed in my heart. I knew that I now wanted to do things God’s way. I knew that my end goal in life was to run the race well and to finish victoriously. That is what has helped me through the years.

On July 31, 2011, I was baptized upon the confession of my faith. The next number of years were definitely not easy. I would even say that at times it seemed to have been harder than in the years before my conversion. Out of respect to others, I don’t feel I can share everything that has happened over the years, but I will try to share several main points. You can imagine that with the walls I had built around myself and the comfort I had found in this, that the years following my conversion were full of ups and downs as I tried to relearn how to relate to other believers and to people in general.

Even though I had reached out to God for forgiveness of my sins and had committed my life to following Him, I had many old habits of relating to others in wrong ways that still needed to be sanctified. Things at home continued to improve but there was still room for progress, which added to the stress. As the years went by, my stress level continued to rise. I didn’t know what to do with it, so I resorted to taking high doses of NoDoz® with an energy drink before I went to bed, trying to get my nerves to relax enough so I could sleep (don’t try this at home, it is dangerous). The next day I would get up and face it all again. One year for most of the year I struggled with thoughts of not wanting to continue on with life. During this time, I had a very close friend who gave me much encouragement. I believe that the regular contact I had with this close friend, the prayers of others, and God’s faithfulness all working together kept me from doing something that I would have later regretted.

I had another close friend who had also gone through a lot but seemed to be finding God’s answers to life’s struggles. We would go out for supper, spending time together talking about life’s struggles. I remember times that I would leave his car and tears would be streaming down his face because he wasn’t sure if I was going to make it. Then he went to the mission field for two years to teach English.

I’m not sure what all was going on in his life but one day we got word that he was missing. Eventually we heard from him; he was okay and was living back in the states again. My heart was torn… One of the few friends that I had, had now turned his back on what he had once believed and on that which he had once tried to convince me of. Yet here I was, still struggling… Why not just give up fighting…? Why not just go live the easy life…? As time went on, I continued to long for love and acceptance. At times the struggle, the aching, and the longing seemed almost unbearable. But I knew deep down that giving up was not what I wanted. It would not get the end result that I wanted. Once more through the encouragement and regular contact with my close friend, the prayers of others, and God’s faithfulness, I continued to press on.

Another young man started taking an interest in my life and we eventually became close friends. He and his wife were a great encouragement to me. Then due to some disagreements with the church, they became dissatisfied and left the church. They threw aside a lot of what they had once stood for. So here I was once again with a close friend that had turned his back on what he had once stood for. What’s the use? Why does life need to be so hard? Maybe I should also give up… But I didn’t want to totally throw God out. Maybe I could find a church that was less strict. Once again, I came to my senses and realized that’s not really what I wanted. That direction wouldn’t take me where I wanted to go. So once more through the encouragement and regular contact with my close friend, the prayers of others, and God’s faithfulness, I continued to press on. At the time it was tough, but looking back, I see I have learned a lot by all I have gone through.

In the fall of 2015, I went to Washington state due to a work opportunity. At the time I went, there were things going on at my home church that I was struggling with. Because of all the stress that I was facing, I was feeling quite discouraged about Church life, Christianity, and life in general. I wasn’t wanting to throw my Christianity away, but I was wondering, “Is this really what it’s all about?” “Why can’t people just get along?” Is this really what God had in mind for His people? If we are “little Christs” like we claim to be, shouldn’t we be able to get along? Shouldn’t we be the ones that are joyful and full of life?

I went to Washington with these kinds of thoughts on my mind. While there, I attended a church that was both Biblical and spiritually minded. It’s hard to explain all that went on in my mind, heart, and life during those six months. But I left there and went back home with a renewed strength and vision.

We should be the light of the world! We should have something to offer others! We should be able to get along with one another! Yes, we do go through hard times individually and collectively as a church, but if we fight the good fight of faith, if we finish our course, if we keep the faith, there is laid up for each of us a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only but unto all them also that love his appearing. I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith: Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing –2 Timothy 4:7-8.

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

June 15, 2018, at 4:40 pm. the scream of the emergency services’ pager split the peaceful afternoon as it crackled to life. “One-car rollover on ‘Gingko Avenue’, possible entrapment,” was the repeated dispatch. As we walked onto the scene, there sat a young girl who appeared to be in her mid-twenties and was visibly banged up. With blood and tears streaming down her face, she repeated these phrases, “I don’t want to die… I’m not ready to die… I may never see my baby again.” As seconds turned to minutes, the paramedics tried to calm her anxious nerves. We searched the mangled car and surrounding area for the supposed missing baby. All the while she sat there with lines of worry and fear. She had tears and blood streaming down her face, as she repeated, “I may never see my baby again… I don’t want to die… I’m not ready to die.”

As first responders, all we found was a car seat that wasn’t fastened in, with no evidence of a baby anywhere. As the ambulance crew strapped her to the stretcher and loaded her in the ambulance, she was still repeating, “Where’s my baby…? I’m not ready to die… I don’t want to die… I may never see my baby again.”

As I left the scene that evening, with that image and those phrases running through my mind, I was struck with two sober thoughts. If that was me, miraculously surviving an accident and sitting there beside my vehicle, barely coherent, with blood streaming down my face, what would I be saying? What would the paramedics and rescue team remember me by? Would I be ready to die? Would I be clear before God?

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

As Christians, when is the last time we helped someone prepare their soul for death? As believers who have been redeemed from the misery and chaos of a life of sin (see 1 Corinthians 6:9-11), we should …be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh [us] you a reason of the hope that is in [us] you with meekness and fear: –1 Peter 3:15.

In the fall of 2018, God opened the door for me to move to a church in a different state where I have found stability. It was here that God brought a godly young lady into my life, and we were married on November 30, 2019. Being married and having brothers who surrounded me with discipleship, compassion, and prayerful support helped me to grow in the Lord in many ways.

Being here has awakened within me a renewed vision to be the light of the world. Today, I am thankful that God did not let me go. As I kept fighting the spiritual fight, God kept giving me the strength and wisdom to do the next right thing. With each victory, my strength has grown stronger. Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you… –James 4:8. I thank God for giving me victory and for helping me find my ultimate source of love, security, and purpose—my Lord and Saviour, Jesus Christ.

نشأت في نفس الكنيسة التي وُلد فيها ونشأ والداي. ومع ذلك، بحلول الوقت الذي بلغت فيه عشر سنوات، بدأ والداي يقلقان من الاتجاه الذي يسلكه الشباب وأرادا شيئًا مختلفًا لأطفالهما. لذا تواصل والداي مع كنيسة من ولاية أخرى، مما ساعدهم على التواصل مع كنيسة صغيرة كانت تقع بالقرب من مكان سكننا.

كنت طفلاً هادئًا ذو إرادة قوية وسرعان ما كنت أتحول إلى مراهق متمرد. فعل والداي كل ما عرفاه ليفعلانه من أجلي في ذلك الوقت. ومن ذلك الانتقال إلى هذه الكنيسة الجديدة لأن فيها بيئة شبابية تقية أكثر. واجهت صعوبة مع هذا التغيير. في كنيستنا القديمة، كان لدي أصدقاء كانوا على نفس موجتي ويدعمونني في طرق تمردي، لكن في الكنيسة الجديدة كنت أكثر من «الفتى السيئ» ولم أتناسب مع الشباب الآخرين.

مع مرور الوقت تلاشت تلك الكنيسة، وقرر والداي الانتقال إلى ولاية أخرى، أقرب إلى كنيسة أكثر استقرارًا. وهكذا، عندما كنت في الرابعة عشرة، أمضينا ليلتنا الأولى في ولاية مختلفة، في بيت مختلف، في طريق مختلف، ومع جيران مختلفين. تَسَوَّقنا في بلدة مختلفة وذهبنا إلى كنيسة مختلفة، مع أشخاص لا أعرفهم تقريبًا. لم أحب التغيير. وجدت صعوبة في لقاء أشخاص جدد وتكوين صداقات جديدة. كافحت بشدة مع كل هذه التغيرات، لذا لم أهتم بمحاولة الاندماج وأن أكون جزءًا فعالًا في حياتنا الجديدة. بدلًا من ذلك، بنيت جدرانًا حول حياتي وقلبي ببطء، وفي نفس الوقت أصبحت أبرد وأكثر تمردًا.

كلما كبرت وأصبحت أكثر قسوة، حاول والداي التعامل معي، لكني لم أرغب في أي شيء من ذلك. في النهاية حصلت على وظيفة وتعرّفت على موسيقى الكانتري وأشياء دنيوية أخرى. وبما أنني كنت أستمتع بالعمل، فقد غرزت نفسي فيه وعملت ساعات طويلة. هكذا لم أكن بحاجة لأن أكون حول العائلة أو الناس في الكنيسة، ولم أكن بحاجة للذهاب إلى نشاطات الكنيسة. وبالتالي، أصبحت أكثر انعزالًا وابتعادًا عن من حولي.

لم يعرف أهل الكنيسة كيف يتعاملون معي؛ معظمهم تركوني لنفسي. لكن في أعماقي كنت أتوق بشدة للمحبة والقبول من عائلتي والكنيسة. أدى ذلك بي إلى الانحدار. واصلت كبت مشاعري وبناء جدار حول نفسي، وفي الوقت نفسه زاد قسوتي في القلب. ومع مرور الوقت، انسحبت أكثر فأكثر من عائلتي والكنيسة. شعرت أكثر فأكثر بأنني شخص غير منسجم اجتماعيًا لا يعرف أحد ما الذي يفعلونه بي. قررت أنني سأهرب وأعيش حياتي الخاصة.

بطريقة ما علم والداي بهذه الفكرة وحاولا فعل كل ما يعلمان أنه يجب فعله لمساعدتي، لكني كنت أستاء من ذلك. بالنظر إلى الوراء، أعلم بيقين أنهما كانا يفعلان ذلك بدافع المحبة والاهتمام، لكن كان هناك نقص كبير في علاقتنا. وهكذا استمررت في أن أصبح أكثر قسوة وبرودًا.

في الصيف الذي كنت فيه في السابعة عشرة، جاء إلى كنيستنا وزير زائر («مايك») وعائلته لعقد اجتماعات. كنت أعرفهم منذ سنوات وسرعان ما بدأ قلبي يلين وينفتح من خلال تفاعلي معهم أثناء الاجتماعات. لست متأكدًا تمامًا لماذا، لكن لسبب ما قررت أنني أريد قضاء فصل الشتاء معهم. فاتصل والداي بهم، وقرّرنا أن أستطيع البقاء معهم لبضعة أشهر.

كانت خطتي أن أقضي بضعة أشهر بعيدًا عن كل شيء ثم أعود إلى المنزل عندما أقترب من الثامنة عشرة. وبمجرد أن أصبح في الثامنة عشرة، كنت أخطط لترك المنزل والقيام بأموري الخاصة. كنت متأكدًا أنه لا أحد يستطيع إيقافي لأنني سأكون في سن الرشد قانونيًا. ولكن، كان لدى الله خطط مختلفة بوضوح...

بطريقة ما أقنعني «مايك» بالذهاب معه لحضور أسبوع من الاجتماعات في ولاية أخرى. بينما كنا هناك، لا أذكر أن الإدانة كانت أقوى من أي وقت آخر. ومع ذلك، في إحدى الأمسيات بعد الخدمة سألني إن كنت أريد أن أصبح مسيحيًا وأن تُغفر خطاياي. لا أذكر ما الذي أخبرته به، لكن تحدثنا لفترة. أخذني عبر الكتاب المقدس، يساعدني على أن أرى ما يقوله الله عن كل ذلك؛ ثم صلّينا. عندما نهضنا من الصلاة، لا أستطيع أن أقول إن شيئًا كبيرًا حدث، لكن بالتأكيد كانت تلك الليلة التي وجدت فيها الخلاص! تلك الليلة تغيّر شيء في قلبي. علمت أنني الآن أريد أن أفعل الأشياء على طريقة الله. علمت أن هدفي النهائي في الحياة هو أن أجري السباق جيدًا وأن أنتهي منتصرًا. هذا ما ساعدني خلال السنين.

في 31 تموز (يوليو) 2011، اعتمدت بعد اعترافي بإيماني. لم تكن السنوات التالية سهلة بالتأكيد. سأقول حتى إنه في أوقات بدا أنها أصعب من السنوات قبل تحويلي. احتراما للآخرين، لا أشعر أنني أستطيع مشاركة كل ما حدث على مر السنين، لكنني سأحاول مشاركة عدة نقاط رئيسية. يمكنك أن تتخيل أنه مع الجدران التي بنيتها حول نفسي والراحة التي وجدتها في ذلك، كانت السنوات التي تلت تحويلي مليئة بالصعود والهبوط بينما كنت أحاول أن أتعلم من جديد كيفية العلاقة مع المؤمنين الآخرين ومع الناس عمومًا.

على الرغم من أنني توسلت إلى الله لمغفرة خطاياي والتزمت حياتي باتباعه، إلا أن لدي عادات قديمة كثيرة في التعامل مع الآخرين بطرق خاطئة كانت لا تزال بحاجة إلى قداسة. استمرت الأمور في البيت بالتحسن ولكن كان هناك مجال للتقدم، مما زاد الضغوط. ومع مرور السنين، استمر مستوى توتري في الارتفاع. لم أكن أعرف ما الذي سأفعله حيال ذلك، لذا لجأت إلى تناول جرعات عالية من NoDoz® مع مشروب طاقة قبل أن أذهب إلى الفراش، محاولًا جعل أعصابي تسترخي بما يكفي لأتمكن من النوم (لا تجرب هذا في المنزل، إنه خطير). في اليوم التالي كنت أستيقظ وأواجه كل ذلك من جديد. في أحد الأعوام، طوال معظم السنة، كنت أُعاني من أفكار عدم الرغبة في الاستمرار في الحياة. خلال هذا الوقت، كان لدي صديق مقرب جدًا منحني الكثير من التشجيع. أعتقد أن التواصل المنتظم الذي كان بيني وبينه، وصلوات الآخرين، وإيمان الله الدائم—كلها عملت معًا لتمنعني من القيام بشيء كنت سأندم عليه لاحقًا.

كان لدي صديق مقرب آخر مر أيضًا بالكثير لكنه بدا وكأنه يجد أجوبة الله لصراعات الحياة. كنا نخرج للعشاء، نقضي وقتًا معًا نتحدث عن صراعات الحياة. أتذكر مرات كنت أغادر سيارته ودموعه تنهمر على وجهه لأنه لم يكن متأكدًا مما إذا كنت سأستمر أم لا. ثم ذهب إلى الميدان التبشيري لمدة عامين ليعلّم الإنجليزية.

لست متأكدًا مما كان يحدث في حياته لكن يومًا ما وصلنا خبر أنه مفقود. في النهاية سمعنا منه؛ كان بخير وكان يعيش في الولايات المتحدة مرة أخرى. تمزق قلبي… أحد القلائل الذين كانوا أصدقائي قد استدار الآن ظهرًا عما كان يؤمن به سابقًا وعن ما كان يحاول أن يقنعني به ذات مرة. ومع ذلك ها أنا، ما زلت أكافح… لماذا لا أستسلم عن القتال…؟ لماذا لا أذهب وأعيش الحياة السهلة…؟ ومع مرور الوقت، استمرت رغبتي في المحبة والقبول. في أحيانٍ كان الكفاح والوجع والاشتياق يكاد يكون لا يطاق. لكني كنت أعلم في أعماقي أن الاستسلام لم يكن ما أريده. لن يصل بي إلى النتيجة النهائية التي أردتها. مرة أخرى من خلال تشجيع ومواظبة التواصل مع صديقي المقرب، وصلوات الآخرين، وإيمان الله الدائم، واصلت التقدم.

بدأ شاب آخر يظهر اهتمامًا بحياتي وأصبحنا في النهاية أصدقاء حميمين. هو وزوجته كانا تشجيعًا كبيرًا لي. ثم بسبب بعض الخلافات مع الكنيسة، أصبحا غير راضيين وغادرا الكنيسة. تخلّيا عن الكثير مما وقفوا من أجله يومًا ما. فها أنا مرة أخرى مع صديق مقرب استدار ظهره عما وقف لأجله من قبل. ما الفائدة؟ لماذا يجب أن تكون الحياة صعبة هكذا؟ ربما يجب عليّ أيضًا أن أستسلم… لكني لم أرد أن أطرد الله تمامًا. ربما أستطيع أن أجد كنيسة أقل تشددًا. مرة أخرى رجعت إلى رشدي وأدركت أن هذا ليس ما أريده حقًا. هذا الاتجاه لن يأخذني إلى حيث أريد أن أذهب. لذا مرة أخرى من خلال تشجيع ومواظبة التواصل مع صديقي المقرب، وصلوات الآخرين، وإيمان الله الدائم، واصلت التقدم. في ذلك الوقت كان الأمر صعبًا، لكن بالنظر إلى الوراء، أرى أنني تعلمت الكثير مما مررت به.

في خريف 2015، ذهبت إلى ولاية واشنطن بسبب فرصة عمل. حين ذهبت، كانت هناك أمور تحدث في كنيستي المنزلية كنت أواجه صعوبة معها. بسبب كل الضغوط التي كنت أواجهها، شعرت بالإحباط بشأن حياة الكنيسة، والمسيحية، والحياة عمومًا. لم أكن أرغب في رمي مسيحيتي بعيدًا، لكنني كنت أتساءل: «هل هذا حقًا كل ما فيه الأمر؟» «لماذا لا يستطيع الناس أن يتعايشوا فقط؟» هل هذا حقًا ما قصده الله لشعبه؟ إذا كنا «مسيحًا صغارًا» كما ندعي، ألا ينبغي أن نكون قادرين على التوافق؟ أليس ينبغي أن نكون نحن الذين نفرح ونكون مملوئين بالحياة؟

The year was around 60 AD. The Apostle Paul had been apprehended and almost killed in the Temple at Jerusalem by a mob of angry Jews.

A few days later, he had been whisked off to the Roman Procurator Felix because of danger from a group of Jewish plotters. Felix had heard his case and though there was no evidence to convict Paul, Felix had kept him in prison for the next two years until the new Procurator, Festus, took his place.

King Herod Agrippa II came to visit Festus and the two of them listened to Paul speak. During the hearing Paul …reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, [until finally] Felix trembled, and answered, Go thy way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for thee –Acts 24:25. Then towards the end of Paul’s oration …Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad –Acts 26:24.

Festus was not speaking of scientific knowledge, but of the fact that Paul was well-studied. Worse yet, Paul was making the governor uncomfortable with his sinful life and his reasoning made clear that the only solution for both Festus and Agrippa was to follow the Scriptures of the Hebrews.

Paul was well educated. He made clear in his letters and sermons, quoting not only from the Jewish Bible, but also from a variety of Greek and Cretan philosophers and poets.

In more modern times, it seems as though science is not a friend to faith. Many scientists claim that the idea of an intelligent designer of the Universe is ludicrous. Further, many of them would say that those who believe such things are the next thing to savages.

It certainly turns many Christians away from science entirely. They do not see something so antagonistic to the fundamental Christian faith as being useful.

I can understand this point of view, but I think that we should not give up learning simply because some of those who claim to be so knowledgeable are, in actuality, quite foolish.

Creation

When I think about the subject of science, I often begin with the subject of creation. This is the beginning of everything and is the first place where “science” and the Bible first come into conflict.

Science is simply unable to accept that there could have been a Creator God who set in motion everything that we see.

There are many books delving into the subject of intelligent design and seeing God’s fingerprints throughout creation. It takes a lot more faith to believe that the universe happened by chance, than to believe in a Creator.

The Bible makes it clear that God was not only present at the time of Creation, but it was also He who began it (John 1:1-3). Paul says For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse –Romans 1:20.

People should be able to discern that there is a Creator God involved in our world and the universe from the time of Creation. They should be able to understand a few other things about Him as well. Perhaps most important for our discussion here, we can tell by looking at creation that God is an orderly God and that He created the world to function with a specific structure and laws that govern it.

This is one of the big differences between the Creation account found in Genesis and the myths of creation found in other cultures of the time. The Bible makes it clear that God intentionally created the world, that He did so in an orderly fashion, and that He made certain that every part of it meshed with all the other parts. There is no magic or mystical thinking in the Genesis account.

The Laws of the Universe Still Stand

There are many people who believe that they can alter the way that the universe functions, that they can behave in immoral ways and not suffer the rewards of sin, and that they can do foolish things and not suffer the consequences of their behavior.

The Prophet Jeremiah tells us that there are laws which are in place that will not cease to function. Thus saith the LORD, which giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night, which divideth the sea when the waves thereof roar; The LORD of hosts is his name: If those ordinances depart from before me, saith the LORD, then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before me for ever –Jeremiah 31:35-36.

There is a whole set of laws that governs the way that the earth rotates on its axis and orbits the sun. Everything from the speed of light to the way that gravity pulls things towards large bodies of mass was instituted at the time of Creation—…all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation –2 Peter 3:4.

Since those laws continue and do not fluctuate, we are able to understand them—at least in part. This is what science is—the study of the natural world that we see and an attempt to comprehend the ways in which it works. God created our world in such a way that if you do an experiment the same way every time, you will get the same results every time.

Science Will Never Understand Everything

The Prophet Isaiah says, For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the LORD. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts –Isaiah 55:8-9.

Even the smartest quantum physicists will admit that they don’t understand everything. In fact, the number of questions that they have is greater than the whole storehouse of knowledge that has been accumulated.

Most of us will have far less understanding of the universe than that. We won’t understand all the details of how the atom functions. We won’t be able to do the calculus necessary to put a satellite into orbit. That’s all right. The important thing is that we learn what we can in order to understand what an amazing and orderly God we serve.

Presuppositions are a Problem

The biggest problem that we see in science is not the science itself, rather it is the biases of the people performing the science. The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God… –Psalm 14:1. By this definition, many scientists are fools.

I don’t say this lightly. Atheists observe the universe and since they believe that there cannot be a God, they must then explain how it exists without the presence of an actual Creator. This is the heart of foolishness.

When they come to gaps in their knowledge, they are silent and yet the Christian can explain them in a few simple words. As I said before, when we look at the complexity of the universe, from the tiniest things to the largest galaxies, we can see the hands of God at work.

When I consider thy heavens, the work of thy fingers, the moon and the stars, which thou hast ordained; What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of man, that thou visitest him? –Psalm 8:3-4. When we think about the world around us, when we read what scientists write, it is crucial that we come to it with a knowledge that God is behind all of this. For in him we live, and move, and have our being… – Acts 17:28, and nothing that science can discern will change that.

Science should be like a detective, uncovering God’s fingerprints on the universe, not someone bound and determined to discredit His very real presence.

Many Scientists Believe in God

Looking into the past, many scientists were men who believed in the God of the Bible. Isaac Newton, Francis Bacon, Nicholas Copernicus and many others believed in the Bible and were forthright in their expression of this faith to others.

In more modern days, there are many men and women of science who believe in the God of the Bible. Just because one is working in science doesn’t mean that they are unable to have a life of faith.

Many people have co-opted scientific discoveries to push messages that are against Christian belief and teaching.

We need to remember that when there is a set of facts, there are usually different explanations that can account for their presence. Creation and evolution examine the same facts of nature, yet from a different perspective or bias, thus they end up with vastly different conclusions. Perhaps it is a little like a Sherlock Holmes story, where Dr. Watson routinely takes the facts and gives an inaccurate explanation of them, while the detective takes the same information and gives the right explanation.

Science and Medicine

It is not against Scripture to research how things work in our universe, as long as we do so within a Biblical framework and understanding that there is a Creator God who is ordering it all.

Modern medicine is an application of many various fields, including anatomy, microanatomy, genetics, and biochemistry. The point, in this case, is to observe the human body the best that we can and then to fix the things that go wrong with it. Doctors can be scientists, but most of them are simply applying knowledge which has been passed down to them through their training.

Observation is where things start. Let’s consider diabetes as an example. Aretaeus of Cappadocia in the second century AD was the first person to give a complete description of diabetes and actually gave the disease the name diabetes. The problem was that while he was able to diagnose people with this illness, he had no treatment to help his patients. Observation had only taken him so far.

Over time, other work was done that demonstrated that the problem was an issue in the pancreas and that something was specifically wrong with the islet cells. Even into the early 1900s, there was no cure for Diabetes Mellitus and the only solution that doctors had to offer was an extremely low glycemic diet with severe calorie limits—attempting to keep patients at 500 or 600 calories a day. As can be imagined, this wasn’t an ideal treatment.

It wasn’t until the 1920s that a couple of researchers in Canada discovered a way to extract insulin from dogs and administered it to a 14-year-old who was dying of diabetes. The extract saved his life and began a new era for people with diabetes.

This is the way that things work. We begin by observing a disease and various medications that seem to be effective for it, then over time and through meticulous testing we can assess what treatments are most effective for that illness.

Studies in which half of the participants with a disease are given a medication or treatment and half are given a placebo (a pill without medical efficacy) are still the most effective way of telling whether something really works.

Why Treatments Need to be Studied

There is a real tendency to believe that the things that you have been taught are effective. We know that George Washington died of pneumonia. His doctors probably damaged his chances of recovery by bleeding him four times for a total of close to 40 percent of his blood volume. They probably would have bled him a fifth time, but he wasn’t thought to be strong enough to survive the procedure.

Doctors bled patients because they believed that there were toxic build ups in the blood stream that had to be let out. Most of the people who died after bloodletting would probably have died anyway, but bleeding people who are really sick certainly doesn’t help them recover.

Maybe the doctors simply wanted to be doing something. Patients expected bloodletting and so they met those expectations, even though it harmed the patients.

Experience is what lets you make the same mistakes with a lot more confidence.

What Makes a Good Study

Good studies—have plenty of patients in them, have a control group (that either receives an inactive pill called a placebo, or the current best treatment for that disease), and have the test group getting the new treatment. It is also important for the control group and the test group to be matched as closely as possible. Finally, the size of the groups in the study is vital to the conclusions of the study. If there are only ten or twenty patients in the study, it is not a large enough group to really sort out if something works or doesn’t.

For many diseases there is something called a placebo effect. This placebo effect is when people get better from an illness even though they are not receiving something that should be effective at treating the malady. Interestingly, in studies, many people get side effects from the inert pills. If 20 percent of the people getting the placebo get better and 45 percent of the people getting the treatment get better, that would indicate that the treatment is effective. If the difference is minimal—say 20 percent of the placebo group and 23 percent of the treatment group improve—then the treatment isn’t effective.

Problems

The biggest problem with many treatments is that they simply aren’t studied. Vitamin supplements and herbal compounds may work, but many of them have never actually been studied in a trial comparing them with a control group. Most of the information is anecdotal. The fact that someone’s grandmother or uncle benefited from something is possibly an indication that it is effective, but it doesn’t tell us how effective this treatment is or what dosage level is ideal.

Another issue is when studies simply don’t have enough participants to really give accurate information. Many studies only include ten or twenty patients. That is simply not enough to identify how well a treatment works or what side effects can be expected. For a drug to be approved by the FDA, it will typically have been studied on between 1,000 to 3,000 patients with the disease.

A final issue with studies is when they show that a medication is effective, but the effect isn’t clinically significant. As an example, a new injectable medication for dementia (aducanumab) was recently approved by the FDA. It is very expensive, and the benefit seemed to be small. Patients who were on it got an average of 1.5 more test questions right on an 85-question mental status questionnaire after 18 months compared to the control group.

One can rightly question if the benefits shown by this medication are worth the 50,000 dollar-per-year cost. More than that, how much of a meaningful improvement in someone’s everyday activities would come from using such a medicine? It seems unlikely that it would make very much of a difference.

It is unfortunate, but drug companies will always try to make it seem like their medicine is the best, even if the studies do not show significant benefit over existing, cheaper options.

Conclusion

Christians are faced with a world which does not love them or their beliefs. Many would try to use science as a way to bludgeon them into giving up their faith. I hope that does not lead us to give up on the scientific method or to give up attempting to understand the laws behind the universe that God created.

The scientific method is valid, even if many of the people who use it are atheists or agnostics. If a treatment works, it should be observable, testable, and repeatable.

Even as we approach it, we have a basic understanding of the universe that atheists don’t have. Knowing that there is a Creator God who loves us makes a major difference as we interpret the results of all the different observations that are being made in the fields of medicine and other places.

Those who do not know God are bound to be ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth –2 Timothy 3:7. On the other hand, if we begin with a Biblical understanding, we can use science as a tool to help us to understand the creation that He has placed around us.
